Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities Venkataramanaswamy S.V. inaugurating the third AIISH International Audiology Convention in Mysuru on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: M.A. Sriram
The two-day third AIISH International Audiology Convention (AIISH – IAC 3) organised by the All India Institute of Speech and Hearing (AIISH) began in Mysuru on Wednesday.
Inaugurating the convention, Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities Venkataramanaswamy S.V. said early detection of hearing disorders and timely intervention are essential.
The theme of the convention, “Auditory Electrophysiology”, is highly significant in the present healthcare scenario, he said.
He said hearing is one of the most important senses through which human beings communicate, learn, interact, and participate in society. Hearing impairment can affect not only communication but also education, employment, social relationships, and the overall quality of life of an individual.
Auditory electrophysiology plays an important role in understanding the functioning of the auditory system. Scientific developments in this field have helped professionals assess hearing functions, identify hearing-related problems at an early stage, and plan appropriate interventions, he explained.
“I believe that the exchange of scientific knowledge, clinical experiences and research findings through conventions like this will strengthen our healthcare and rehabilitation systems,” he felt.
He added: “As the Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities, I would like to emphasise one important aspect – the rights, dignity and inclusion of persons with disabilities.”
“Let us work together towards building a society where every individual, irrespective of disability, is respected, empowered and given equal opportunities,” he said.
He said AIISH is a premier institution, dedicated to education, research, clinical services and the rehabilitation of individuals with communication disorders.
The Commissioner said discussions, research presentations and professional interactions during these two days of the international conference lead to new developments in audiology and better opportunities for persons with hearing and communication disabilities.
Delegates from across the country are attending the convention. The convention featured oral and poster sessions, interaction of students and researchers with experts. The convention also features talks by experts from India and abroad on topics such as auditory electrophysiology, diagnostics and rehabilitation and clinical practice.
